subjects.name: SQL
subjects.description: Complete SQL preparation from fundamentals to placement-level query solving.

topics.title: SQL Fundamentals
topics.learn: SQL is used to query and manipulate data stored in relational databases. Understand databases, tables, rows, columns and the basic structure of a SQL statement.

topics.title: SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY
topics.learn: Use SELECT to retrieve columns, WHERE to filter rows and ORDER BY to sort the result.
topics.example: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000 ORDER BY salary DESC;

topics.title: DISTINCT, LIMIT and Filtering
topics.learn: Use DISTINCT to eliminate duplicate results and LIMIT to control the number of returned rows.
topics.example: SELECT DISTINCT department FROM employees LIMIT 10;

topics.title: Aggregate Functions and GROUP BY
topics.learn: Aggregate functions calculate values across multiple rows. GROUP BY creates groups on which aggregates can be calculated.
topics.example: SELECT department, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department;

topics.title: HAVING
topics.learn: HAVING filters grouped results after aggregation, while WHERE filters individual rows before grouping.
topics.example: SELECT department, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

topics.title: INNER JOIN
topics.learn: INNER JOIN combines rows from related tables when the join condition matches.
topics.example: SELECT e.name, d.name FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id;

topics.title: LEFT, RIGHT and FULL JOIN
topics.learn: Outer joins preserve rows that do not have a matching row on the other side.
topics.example: SELECT customers.name, orders.id FROM customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id;

topics.title: Subqueries
topics.learn: A subquery is a query nested inside another query and can be used for filtering, comparison or derived results.
topics.example: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

topics.title: CTEs
topics.learn: Common Table Expressions make complex queries easier to read by defining temporary named result sets.
topics.example: WITH high_paid AS (SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 80000) SELECT * FROM high_paid;

topics.title: Window Functions
topics.learn: Window functions perform calculations across related rows without collapsing them into groups.
topics.example: SELECT name, salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank FROM employees;

topics.title: Constraints and Data Integrity
topics.learn: Constraints enforce rules that keep relational data valid and consistent.
topics.example: CREATE TABLE users (id INT PRIMARY KEY, email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL);

topics.title: Indexes
topics.learn: Indexes improve lookup performance by providing a faster access path to rows, while also adding storage and write overhead.

topics.title: Transactions and ACID
topics.learn: Transactions group database operations into a logical unit. ACID describes important transaction properties.
topics.example: BEGIN; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE id = 1; COMMIT;

topics.title: Normalization
topics.learn: Normalization organizes relational data to reduce unnecessary duplication and update anomalies.
topics.example: Separate customer details from order details instead of repeating customer information for every order.

topics.title: Placement SQL Practice
topics.learn: Solve common placement queries involving joins, grouping, subqueries, ranking and analytical calculations.
topics.example: Find the second-highest salary, department-wise employee counts and employees earning more than their department average.

subjects.name: JavaScript
subjects.description: Structured JavaScript preparation from fundamentals to interview-level concepts.

topics.title: JavaScript Fundamentals
topics.learn: Understand how JavaScript runs, where it is used and the basic syntax used to write programs.

topics.title: Variables and Data Types
topics.learn: Learn let, const, primitive values and reference values.

topics.title: Operators and Type Conversion
topics.learn: Understand arithmetic, comparison, logical and assignment operators and the difference between implicit and explicit conversion.

topics.title: Conditions and Loops
topics.learn: Use conditional statements and loops to control program execution.

topics.title: Functions
topics.learn: Functions organize reusable behavior and can be declared, expressed or written as arrow functions.

topics.title: Scope and Closures
topics.learn: Understand lexical scope, block scope and how inner functions can remember variables from outer scopes.

topics.title: Arrays
topics.learn: Learn common array operations and functional methods used heavily in application code and interviews.

topics.title: Objects
topics.learn: Objects store related data and behavior using properties and methods.

topics.title: DOM and Events
topics.learn: Understand how JavaScript interacts with HTML through the DOM and responds to user events.

topics.title: Promises and Async JavaScript
topics.learn: Asynchronous JavaScript allows operations such as network calls to complete without blocking the main flow.

topics.title: Fetch and APIs
topics.learn: Use fetch to communicate with HTTP APIs and process JSON responses.

topics.title: Classes and OOP in JavaScript
topics.learn: JavaScript classes provide syntax for constructing objects and organizing behavior.

topics.title: Modules
topics.learn: Modules let applications divide code into reusable files using import and export.

topics.title: Error Handling
topics.learn: Use exceptions and structured error handling to make applications more reliable.

topics.title: JavaScript Interview Practice
topics.learn: Review common placement questions covering closures, hoisting, promises, async behavior, arrays and objects.
topics.example: Explain why let and const behave differently from var and describe closure-based examples.

subjects.name: Git & GitHub
subjects.description: Practical version control and GitHub workflow preparation.

topics.title: Git Fundamentals
topics.learn: Git is a distributed version-control system used to track changes in source code.

topics.title: Repository and First Commit
topics.learn: Create a repository, stage files and record the first snapshot.
topics.example: git init && git add . && git commit -m "Initial commit"

topics.title: Git History
topics.learn: Inspect past commits and understand how project history is represented.

topics.title: Branches
topics.learn: Branches allow independent development without changing the main development line.

topics.title: Merge
topics.learn: Merging combines changes from one branch into another.
topics.example: git switch main && git merge feature/login

topics.title: Remote Repositories
topics.learn: Remote repositories allow code to be shared and synchronized with services such as GitHub.

topics.title: GitHub Workflow
topics.learn: Understand the common workflow of branches, commits, pushes and pull requests.
topics.example: Create branch → commit changes → push → open pull request → review → merge.

topics.title: Merge Conflicts
topics.learn: Conflicts happen when Git cannot automatically combine competing changes.
topics.example: Resolve conflicting lines, stage the corrected file and continue the merge.

topics.title: Stash
topics.learn: Git stash temporarily stores uncommitted changes so you can switch tasks cleanly.

topics.title: Reset and Revert
topics.learn: Reset changes repository state while revert creates a new commit that reverses an earlier commit.

topics.title: Tags and Releases
topics.learn: Tags identify important points in project history and are commonly used for releases.

topics.title: Git Interview Practice
topics.learn: Review the Git questions commonly asked in development interviews.
topics.example: Explain the difference between merge and rebase, reset and revert, fetch and pull.

subjects.name: REST APIs
subjects.description: Web API fundamentals and practical REST API development concepts.

topics.title: HTTP Fundamentals
topics.learn: HTTP defines how clients and servers communicate using requests and responses.

topics.title: Resources and URLs
topics.learn: REST APIs model application entities as resources identified through URLs.

topics.title: HTTP Methods
topics.learn: HTTP methods communicate the intended operation on a resource.

topics.title: Status Codes
topics.learn: HTTP status codes communicate the result of a request.
topics.example: 200 OK, 201 Created, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error.

topics.title: Headers and JSON
topics.learn: Headers carry metadata while JSON is a common representation for API request and response bodies.

topics.title: CRUD APIs
topics.learn: CRUD maps common application operations to API endpoints.

topics.title: Validation and Errors
topics.learn: APIs should validate incoming data and return predictable error responses.

topics.title: Authentication and Authorization
topics.learn: Authentication establishes identity while authorization controls what an authenticated user can access.

topics.title: Pagination Filtering and Sorting
topics.learn: Large datasets should normally be requested in controlled pages with filtering and sorting options.

topics.title: Idempotency
topics.learn: Idempotent operations produce the same intended result when repeated with the same request.
topics.example: PUT /users/42 with the same representation can be safely retried by a client.

topics.title: API Versioning
topics.learn: Versioning allows APIs to evolve without immediately breaking existing clients.

topics.title: REST API Interview Practice
topics.learn: Review endpoint design, status codes, authentication, idempotency and API architecture questions.
topics.example: Design an API for users, orders and payments and explain your endpoint choices.

subjects.name: Linux
subjects.description: Practical Linux command-line and system fundamentals for technical interviews.

topics.title: Linux and the Shell
topics.learn: Linux provides a Unix-like operating-system environment. The shell lets users interact with the system through commands.

topics.title: Filesystem Navigation
topics.learn: Navigate Linux directories and understand the hierarchical filesystem.

topics.title: Files and Directories
topics.learn: Create, copy, move, rename and remove files and directories.

topics.title: Permissions
topics.learn: Linux permissions control who can read, write and execute files.

topics.title: Users and Groups
topics.learn: Linux supports multiple users and groups with separate ownership and permissions.

topics.title: Processes
topics.learn: Processes are running programs managed by the operating system.

topics.title: Pipes and Redirection
topics.learn: Pipes connect command output to another command, while redirection sends output to files.

topics.title: grep, find and Text Processing
topics.learn: Command-line tools make it possible to search and process large amounts of text quickly.

topics.title: Packages
topics.learn: Package managers install, update and remove software packages.

topics.title: Networking Commands
topics.learn: Linux provides command-line utilities for checking network interfaces, connectivity and ports.

topics.title: Services and Logs
topics.learn: Linux systems run background services and maintain logs useful for troubleshooting.

topics.title: Shell Scripting Basics
topics.learn: Shell scripts automate repeated administrative and development tasks.

subjects.name: System Design
subjects.description: Placement-oriented system design from fundamentals to complete high-level designs.

topics.title: What is System Design?
topics.learn: System design is the process of deciding how software components, data stores and communication mechanisms work together to satisfy requirements.
topics.example: Design a URL shortener that accepts a long URL and returns a short URL.

topics.title: Functional and Non-Functional Requirements
topics.learn: Functional requirements describe what the system does. Non-functional requirements describe qualities such as availability, latency and scalability.
topics.example: A chat application must deliver messages; it may also require low latency and high availability.

topics.title: Capacity Estimation
topics.learn: Estimate users, requests, storage and bandwidth before selecting architecture.
topics.example: Estimate daily active users, requests per second and storage growth for a social application.

topics.title: Client Server Architecture
topics.learn: Most applications separate clients from backend services that handle business logic and data access.

topics.title: API Design
topics.learn: Design clear APIs that expose resources and operations while remaining stable for clients.

topics.title: Load Balancing
topics.learn: A load balancer distributes incoming traffic across multiple backend instances.
topics.example: Client → Load Balancer → Server A / Server B / Server C

topics.title: Caching
topics.learn: Caches keep frequently accessed data closer to applications to reduce latency and database load.

topics.title: SQL vs NoSQL
topics.learn: Database selection depends on data shape, consistency, query needs, scale and operational requirements.
topics.example: A transactional banking system and a flexible high-scale content system may have different database requirements.

topics.title: Replication
topics.learn: Replication keeps multiple copies of data to improve availability, read scalability or fault tolerance.

topics.title: Partitioning and Sharding
topics.learn: Partitioning divides data so large datasets can be distributed across machines.
topics.example: Users can be distributed by user ID ranges or hash buckets.

topics.title: Message Queues
topics.learn: Queues decouple producers and consumers and allow asynchronous work to be processed reliably.

topics.title: CAP and Consistency
topics.learn: Distributed systems involve trade-offs between consistency, availability and partition tolerance, with practical designs choosing behavior appropriate to the use case.
topics.example: A shopping-cart system may tolerate temporary consistency differences differently from a financial ledger.

topics.title: CDN and Rate Limiting
topics.learn: CDNs serve content closer to users, while rate limiting protects services from excessive request volume.
topics.example: User → CDN → Application, with an API gateway applying request limits.

topics.title: Reliability and Fault Tolerance
topics.learn: Reliable systems expect failures and use retries, timeouts, redundancy, graceful degradation and health checks.
topics.example: If a downstream service fails, the application can retry with limits and return a degraded response where appropriate.

topics.title: Observability
topics.learn: Logs, metrics and traces help developers understand system behavior and diagnose failures.
topics.example: Track request latency, error rate and service traces across multiple backend services.

topics.title: System Security
topics.learn: System design must consider authentication, authorization, encryption, secrets and abuse prevention.
topics.example: API gateway performs authentication while services enforce authorization rules.

topics.title: URL Shortener Design
topics.learn: Design a service that maps long URLs to short identifiers and redirects users efficiently.
topics.example: POST /shorten → short code → GET /abc123 → original URL.

topics.title: Chat System Design
topics.learn: Design real-time messaging with message storage, delivery, online presence and scalable communication channels.
topics.example: Client → WebSocket gateway → message service → persistent store.

topics.title: Social Feed Design
topics.learn: Design a feed system that retrieves and ranks content efficiently for a large user base.
topics.example: User posts → content service → feed generation → cache → clients.

topics.title: System Design Interview Practice
topics.learn: Practice the complete design process: clarify requirements, estimate scale, propose architecture, identify bottlenecks and explain trade-offs.
topics.example: Design a video streaming platform from requirements through scalable architecture.
